name: Unterperfuss
kurzbeschreibung: Tiniest municipality in the Innsbruck-Land district, with a rural charm and views of the Stubaier Alpen.
beschreibung:
Overview

Unterperfuss is situated at an elevation of 596 meters in the Tyrolean Inn Valley, approximately twelve kilometers west of Innsbruck, right at the confluence of the Melach River with the Inn. Covering merely 2.28 square kilometers with roughly 240 inhabitants, this picturesque village is the smallest municipality by land area in the district of Innsbruck-Land and the smallest in the entire Inn Valley. The quiet valley floor is defined by broad meadows and centuries-old farmsteads, framed to the south by the foothills of the Sellraintal and the Stubai Alps. Across Tyrol and beyond, Unterperfuss is celebrated as a distinguished equestrian hub, boasting top-tier riding centers, indoor arenas, turnout paddocks, and scenic riding trails weaving through protected riverside woods.

History

The locality was first documented in 1312 in the regional tax register, which recorded Ulrich of 'Nidern Peruens' and his brother Albrecht paying tithes to the court of Hörtenberg. The name originates from a pre-Roman toponym, sharing its linguistic roots with neighboring Oberperfuss. Due to its strategic position at the river junction, Unterperfuss functioned for centuries as a vital ferry crossing over the Inn. This historical role is commemorated by the heritage-listed Ansitz Ferklehen mansion—popularly called the Unterperfer Schlössl—named after the ancient ferrymen ('Fergen') who held sovereign ferry rights and toll privileges. The architectural heart of the village is the filial Church of Saint Catherine of Alexandria: this graceful Rococo chapel was built between 1761 and 1771 by master builder Franz Singer from Götzens. Its interior features exquisite Rococo stucco work and 1761 ceiling frescoes painted by Anton Kirchebner, depicting scenes from the life of Saint Catherine.

Getting There

By car, Unterperfuss is reached via the Inntal Autobahn A12 by taking the Zirl-Ost/Kematen exit and following roads L11 and L233 for about two minutes; travel time from Innsbruck is roughly twelve minutes. Rail travelers take S-Bahn lines S1 or S2 from Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof to the nearby stations of Kematen in Tirol or Zirl, both situated about 1.5 to 2 kilometers away. From these stations, regional VVT buses and gentle walking or cycling paths connect directly into the village.

Tips

Equestrian enthusiasts will appreciate the riding stables of Unterperfuss, offering expert riding instruction, horse boarding, and regional competitions. Cyclists can join the level Inn Cycle Path (Innradweg R3), which runs along the riverbanks and provides scenic, family-friendly riding toward Innsbruck or upstream toward Telfs. Peaceful walking trails trace the Melach river embankment and the riparian woodlands where the Melach meets the Inn. Nearby excursions include the historic Kaiser-Max-Grotte cave on the Martinswand cliff and scenic hikes on the Rangger Köpfl in Oberperfuss.
